Mathematical Genealogy

Advisor-student lineage of the Top 100

Every PhD mathematician has an advisor, and every advisor has an advisor. The Mathematics Genealogy Project catalogs this lineage globally. We use it to identify researchers who are not in the algorithmic Top 100 by publication count but who are tightly connected to the Top 100 through advisor-student relationships.

How the genealogy graph is built

For each Top 100 researcher we look up their MGP record and pull their full advisor and descendant tree. The union of these trees forms a single graph where:

  • Nodes are individual mathematicians (each with a unique MGP id).
  • Edges are advisor-student relationships.
  • The Top 100 are the canonical seeds.
  • Everyone else in the graph is an outsider.

Outsiders are then ranked by their network proximity to the canonical set. Six outsiders qualify as close relations under our cutoff (Personalized PageRank above the canonical-seed median).

Notes on these six

  • Saburô Uchiyama (Japan): an analytic number theorist whose work covered the distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions and integers representable as sums of two squares. He is the doctoral advisor of Koichi Kawada, which places him directly beside the Top 100.
  • Anatoly Karatsuba (Moscow, 1962): foundational Russian number theorist; exponential sums and zeta function zeros. The fast Karatsuba multiplication algorithm also bears his name. Deceased 2008.
  • Olli Järviniemi (Turku, 2023): young Finnish number theorist with a recent PhD; the genealogy graph picks him up via close ties to Matomäki and Tao.
  • Russell Sherman Lehman (Stanford, 1954): older generation, computed early numerical tables in analytic number theory.
  • Robert Tijdeman (Amsterdam, 1969): Dutch number theorist, long based at Leiden. His 1976 theorem that Catalan's equation has only finitely many solutions was a major step toward the proof of Catalan's conjecture.
  • Pan Chengdong (潘承洞) (Peking, 1961): one of the founders of the Chinese Goldbach school; student of Hua Luogeng; major work on Goldbach in the 1960s-70s.
